subject.title: improve(android): make Wear store releases reproducible

question: Should the Android release contract continue accepting previously valid phone version-code suffixes 50–99, and if so what paired-Wear mapping preserves compatibility without reintroducing collisions?
rationale: The branch intentionally changes a previously accepted release identity range, so choosing between compatibility preservation, a migration, or a new issuance-only rule is a release-policy decision rather than a mechanical correction.

options.title: Preserve legacy codes
options.body: Retain acceptance for existing 50–99 phone codes and constrain only newly issued paired phone/Wear codes with explicit tests.

options.title: Adopt the narrower range
options.body: Make 01–49 mandatory only with a documented migration and operator guidance for already-valid 50–99 release metadata.

options.title: Pause the range change
options.body: Land provenance improvements separately and defer version-code policy until the Android release owner confirms the upgrade contract.

recommendation.title: Preserve legacy codes
recommendation.body: Retain acceptance for existing 50–99 phone codes and constrain only newly issued paired phone/Wear codes with explicit tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged Wear companion architecture and its release packaging context make this the strongest available routing candidate for the paired-version policy.
